sentence: É importante os alunos chegarem cedo.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses Bare Phrase Structure: merged objects inherit the category of their projecting head, without predefined phrase templates or bar levels. The evaluative adjective takes the infinitival proposition as its complement; that proposition is the semantic subject of the evaluation. The matrix clause has a silent, nonreferential expletive. Chegar is treated as unaccusative, so os alunos will originate as its internal argument rather than as an agent introduced by little v. The supplied words are retained as whole-word lexical terminals: chegarem is the personal-infinitive form, and É is the finite copular form. Silent T heads represent their grammatical features without requiring a separate morphological segmentation of either word. The silent infinitival C will identify a propositional infinitival clause, while the two silent little-v heads provide nonagentive verbal structure.
derivationStages.statement: Select the lexical and functional objects for the finite evaluative clause and its personal-infinitival clause.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First, the definite determiner merges with alunos, forming the plural nominal argument. Chegarem merges with that nominal as its internal argument and assigns it the Theme role: the students are the entities arriving. Cedo then adjoins to the resulting V object and modifies the arrival event, not the matrix evaluation. Nonagentive little v merges above this structure, and infinitival T merges above little v. T agrees with the accessible nominal argument, obtaining third-person plural features and licensing its nominative Case. This is the personal-infinitive configuration that permits the overt subject os alunos; an obligatorily controlled, uninflected infinitive is not assumed.
derivationStages.statement: Build the embedded verbal domain and establish personal-infinitival agreement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded verb internally merges with infinitival T from the V position shown in the preceding workspace. In the nonagentive verbal domain adopted here, little v has no independent attracting head feature, so the verb raises directly to T. The resulting complex head connects the infinitival verb with the T that has already agreed with os alunos. The higher verb occurrence is pronounced as chegarem; the lower occurrence retains its lexical content but is silent. This is head movement, not the introduction of another arrival predicate. The nominal argument remains in its original position at this stage, keeping head movement distinct from the subsequent subject movement.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the personal-infinitive verb to embedded T.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Os alunos internally merges at the edge of the embedded T object from the internal-argument position already present in the preceding workspace. This satisfies the subject-position requirement of personal-infinitival T and produces the order os alunos chegarem cedo. The higher nominal occurrence is pronounced, while the lower nominal and its terminals are silent copies. The Theme interpretation and nominative licensing remain connected to the lower argument occurrence established earlier. Silent infinitival C then merges with the completed T object, identifying a declarative infinitival proposition. No overt complementizer or controlled PRO is inserted: the overt plural nominal is the infinitival subject.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the embedded subject and complete the infinitival proposition.

values.interpretation: The proposition that the students arrive early is important.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Importante merges with the infinitival clause as its propositional complement: what is evaluated as important is the students' arriving early. This analysis therefore generates the postadjectival clause in place rather than moving it rightward from a previously occupied matrix subject position. The copula merges with the resulting A object, providing the verbal support for adjectival predication. Nonagentive matrix little v merges above the copular domain, and the silent expletive merges at its edge without receiving a thematic role. Finite T then merges above this domain and agrees with the expletive in third-person singular, licensing its nominative Case. Matrix singular agreement consequently does not target the embedded plural subject. The clause expresses a present-tense evaluation, whereas the embedded arrival has infinitival rather than independent finite tense.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix evaluative predicate and establish finite agreement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The copula internally merges with finite T from the verbal position established in the preceding workspace. As in the embedded nonagentive domain, little v has no independent head-attracting feature in this analysis. The higher copular occurrence is pronounced as É, and its lower occurrence is silent. The resulting complex T head places the finite copula before importante and the infinitival proposition. Because É is retained as a whole-word terminal, this movement requires no realization group combining separate morphological terminals.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the finite copula to matrix T.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The silent expletive internally merges at the matrix T edge from its previously established position at the edge of little v. This satisfies the matrix subject-position requirement without moving os alunos out of the infinitival clause. Both expletive occurrences remain unpronounced. The completed derivation thus distinguishes matrix third-person singular agreement from embedded third-person plural agreement, and it interprets cedo inside the arrival predicate. Pronouncing only the designated higher verbal and nominal occurrences yields exactly É importante os alunos chegarem cedo. The final period is sentence punctuation, not an additional item in the supplied token list.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix subject configuration and the analysis of the sentence.
